[[File:Ceratophyllum submersum.jpg|thumb|''Ceratophyllum submersum'']]

'''''Ceratophyllum submersum''''', commonly known as the '''soft hornwort''' or '''tropical hornwort''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/32132|title=PlantFiles: Coontail, Tropical Hornwort, Soft Hornwort|website=Dave's Garden|language=en|access-date=2019-12-11}}</ref> is a species of ''[[Ceratophyllum]]''. It is a submerged, free-floating [[aquatic plant]].<ref>[http://www.ukwildflowers.com/Web_pages/ceratophyllum_submersum_soft_hornwort.htm soft hornwort] UK wildflowers</ref> It has been reported from [[Europe]], [[Central Asia]], northern [[Africa]], scattered places in tropical [[Africa]], [[Turkey]], [[Oman]], [[Florida]], and the [[Dominican Republic]].<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=36951 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>Dobignard, A. & Chatelain, C. (2011). Index synonymique de la flore d'Afrique du nord 3: 1-449. Éditions des conservatoire et jardin botaniques, Genève.</ref><ref>Sheremetova, S.A., Ebel, A.L. & Buko, T.E. (2011). Supplement to the flora of Kemerovo region since 2001 till 2010. Turczaninowia 14(1): 65-74.</ref><ref>Lazkov, G.A. & Sultanova, B.A. (2011). Checklist of vascular plants of Kyrgyzstan. Norrlinia 24: 1-166.</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.5479/si.0081024x.98.1|title=Catalogue of Seed Plants of the West Indies|journal=Smithsonian Contributions to Botany|volume=98|pages=1–1192|year=2012|last1=Acevedo-Rodríguez|first1=Pedro|last2=Strong|first2=Mark T.|hdl=10088/17551}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1080/00837792.2012.10670909|title=Contribution to the Flora of Central-Southern Dhofar (Sultanate of Oman)|journal=Webbia|volume=67|pages=65–91|year=2012|last1=Mosti|first1=Stefano|last2=Raffaelli|first2=Mauro|last3=Tardelli|first3=Marcello|hdl=2158/654870|s2cid=128491512|hdl-access=free}}</ref> It is similar to the submerged [[macrophyte]] ''[[Ceratophyllum demersum]]'', a congeneric plant that is found in most regions of the world.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Nagengast|first1=Barbara|last2=Gąbka|first2=Maciej|date=January 2017|title=Apparent niche partitioning of two congeneric submerged macrophytes in small water bodies: The case of Ceratophyllum demersum L. and C. submersum L.|journal=Aquatic Botany|volume=137|pages=1–8|doi=10.1016/j.aquabot.2016.11.001|issn=0304-3770}}</ref>

== Description ==
The ''C. submersum,'' is a free floating aquatic plant which forks from stem three to four times and ends have 6 to 8 threadlike tips.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.flowgrow.de/db/aquaticplants/ceratophyllum-submersum|title=Ceratophyllum submersum|website=Flowgrow|language=en|access-date=2019-12-11}}</ref> The temperature tolerance is suggested to be between {{Convert|4 to 30|C}}, the optimal temperature is noted to be {{Convert|15 to 30|C}}.<ref name=":3" /> The height of the plant is often 6–12 in. (15–30 cm) or 12–18 in. (30–45 cm).<ref name=":2" />

==Identification==
Soft hornwort and [[rigid hornwort]] (''Ceratophyllum demersum'') can look very similar, despite the difference in texture that is apparent in mature plants. To confirm which species is present, one should check the number of times the leaves divide: just one or two times in rigid hornwort, versus three or four times in soft hornwort.<ref name=Stace>{{cite book |last1=Stace |first1=C.A. |title=New Flora of the British Isles |date=2019 |location=Suffolk |publisher=C&M Floristics |edition=4th |isbn=978-1-5272-2630-2}}</ref>
[[File:Ceratophyllum submersum sl28.jpg|thumb|none|The leaves of soft hornwort are usually branched three or four times, resulting in 8–16 terminal segments.]]

== Habitat ==
''C. submersum'' prefers to colonize [[eutrophic]] waters around agricultural systems.<ref name=":0" /> ''C. submersum'' is a self-regulating rapid grower like ''Ceratophyllum demersum.'' It strives in a moderately lit environment. In a strong lighted environment ''C. submersum'' attains an auburn color tint.<ref name=":3" />  Since this aquatic plant has a fast growth it has to be trimmed often, or at least be provided a larger tank or environment to accommodate it for proper function.<ref name=":3" /> It is found submerged in freshwater<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/113128|title=Ceratophyllum submersum|website=www.cabi.org|access-date=2019-12-11}}</ref> in tropical regions of the world, with the [[Invasive species|species being introduced]] in newer areas around the world, such as [[Ireland]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Smith|first1=S. J.|last2=Wolfe-Murphy|first2=S. A.|date=1991|title=Ceratophyllum submersum L. Soft Hornwort, a Species New to Ireland|journal=The Irish Naturalists' Journal|volume=23|issue=9|pages=374–376|issn=0021-1311|jstor=25539572}}</ref> It has been found in the [[Rosetta]] branch of the [[Nile|Nile River]] of Egypt, where it thrives in either various locations at different times of the year.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=El-Sheekh|first1=Mostafa M.|last2=Haroon|first2=Amany M.|last3=Sabae|first3=Soad|date=2018-09-01|title=Seasonal and spatial variation of aquatic macrophytes and phytoplankton community at El-Quanater El-Khayria River Nile, Egypt|journal=Beni-Suef University Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences|volume=7|issue=3|pages=344–352|doi=10.1016/j.bjbas.2018.03.002|issn=2314-8535|doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== Ecology ===
Its presence in waters have been associated with a decrease in nitrogen forms such NH<sub>4</sub> and NO<sub>3</sub> in water, but an increase in [[pH]], conductivity and [[Oxygen saturation|dissolved oxygen]].<ref name=":1" /> While ''C. demersum'' has been negatively associated with all [[phytoplankton]] classes, ''C. submersum'' was positively associated with them, [[Chlorophyll a|chlorophyll'' a'']] and [[Cyanobacteria|Cyanophyceae]].<ref name=":1" /> ''C. submersum'' and ''C. demersum'' do not share the same habitat, with the cosmopolitan ''C. demersum'' being more distributed, indicating a similar niches. In some cases, ''C. submersum'' can overtake ''C. demersum'' in one vegetative season in a body of water.<ref name=":0" />

== Human uses ==
''C. submersum'' is often used in aquariums as a way to decrease nitrogen in artificial aquatic systems. However, it is not as common in usage as the ''C. demersum.'' It is propagated by cutting the stem of the plant and placing it in the aquatic system.<ref name=":2" /> After the organic matter is converted to soluble inorganic matter the ''C. submersum'' helps to oxygenates waste water.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uses.plantnet-project.org/en/Ceratophyllum_(PROSEA)|title=Ceratophyllum (PROSEA) - PlantUse English|website=uses.plantnet-project.org|access-date=2019-12-11}}</ref>
